relations.subject: n1ql:rollback-transaction
relations.evidence: The `ROLLBACK TRANSACTION` statement enables you to rollback an ACID transaction. You can rollback the entire transaction, or rollback to a previous savepoint. For more information, see [SQL++ Support for Couchbase Transactions](transactions.md).

notable_absence.finding: Same absence pattern as BEGIN TRANSACTION (see begin-transaction.json): ROLLBACK TRANSACTION carries no access-control gate of any kind - no Capella role, no credential-type restriction, no named privilege. The only prerequisite content is behavioral ('This statement may only be used within a transaction') and a cbq-shell operational note about resetting the transaction ID after a failed transaction. This confirms the transaction-statement family is uniformly ungated across BEGIN/ROLLBACK, consistent with the credential-type/capella-role model applying to keyspace-affecting DDL/DML/DCL statements but not to transaction-control statements.

cross_component_finding: Same shared-source-content pattern as begin-transaction.json: this page links out to server/'s transaction overview ('For an overview of Couchbase transactions, see [Transactions](../../../server/current/learn/data/transactions.md)') rather than any Capella-specific overview page, and closes with a Couchbase blog post link. The transaction-statement family (BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK/SAVEPOINT/SET TRANSACTION) continues to read as shared reference content presented unchanged on the Capella docs tree.
cross_product_finding: Per the cross-round transaction check: no textual evidence on this page connects ROLLBACK TRANSACTION to the Java SDK's distributed-transaction feature (sdk:distributed-transaction). Related Links are exclusively to other SQL++ transaction statements, the server/ overview, and the same Couchbase blog post cited on begin-transaction.md. No SDK cross-reference is present, so no relation is asserted; the open question remains open (as flagged in begin-transaction.json), and this page does not resolve it either way.
